title: Error boundaries, and the fallback the user actually sees

videos.script:
A bug in one small card can take the whole page with it. Today you will watch it happen, and then make sure it never costs more than the card.

{{crash}} First the bug. One exclamation mark tells TypeScript a value is always there. It is not, and when the last session of the week is ticked, the page goes white.

{{boundary}} Then an error boundary. It is a class, the one place React still needs one, and it draws something else when a child throws. Around each card, it turns a white page into one card that says it could not be shown.

{{reset}} A boundary that failed stays failed. You will see three cards stuck after the data was fine again, and fix it with a key.

{{limits}} Then what a boundary cannot see: event handlers, timers, and its own mistakes. So one more goes around the whole app.

{{fix}} And the bug itself, fixed where it lives, with TypeScript's help once the exclamation mark is gone.

{{retry}} Last, the server that does not answer gets a screen with a button that works.
